problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(-7)=2\sqrt{3},\,{f}^{′}(-7)=\sqrt{3},\,g(-7)=5\sqrt{3}\,{g}^{′}(-7)=-4\sqrt{3}
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=-7.$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Product Given the Necessary Data
examples.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | $f'(x)$ | $g'(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $0$ |

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big)$ at $x=0.$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big) = f(x)g'(x)+f'(x)g(x).
$$

At the point where $x=0$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=0} & =f(0){g}^{′}(0)+{f}^{′}(0)g(0) \\  & =1\cdot 0+3\cdot (-2) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
